faultDesign.wrongPlaybook: C0 rejects a loaded identity or Pack asset other than Classic.
faultDesign.inputBypass: C1 requires Pointer Lock plus acknowledged keyboard input and an authority trajectory crossing a Chunk boundary.
faultDesign.mutationWithoutPresentation: C2/C3 require both the authoritative voxel result and a consumed mesh commit on WebGL2.
faultDesign.counterWithoutCausality: Worker and Wasm counters are baselined after fixture setup and must advance with the route's own streaming work; a four-center stream shift must also keep client Chunk resources bounded before the return rebuild.
faultDesign.npcWithoutConsequence: C4 requires one model-free NPC action to start and finish with a changed body position.
faultDesign.reloadWithoutFreshness: C5 requires a new runtime epoch, restored world/inventory/NPC state, and another acknowledged real input.

integratedLegacyBrowserProtection.observation: Real Pointer Lock movement, jump, collision-free settling, authoritative edit presentation, Chunk crossing and save/continue are exercised in one world.
The stamped production artifact must load its admitted Classic Pack, Worker and Wasm bytes; later route work must be completed and consumed.
Real mouse mining, drop pickup, E inventory, visible recipe buttons, hotbar keyboard movement, food, placement, and a buffered wood-sword second combo hit are exercised before restored inventory.
A crafted workbench is placed and opened, then dismantled and picked back into inventory; after restore that inventory item is placed and opened again.
One model-free NPC action has matching start/success events and body movement, and the same character identity remains active after restore.
SEEDLANDS_CLASSIC_BENCHMARK changes sampling mode while retaining this exact scenario and action sequence.

explicitGaps.reason: C0 starts from the hydrated production UI and does not independently prove no-JavaScript first paint or pre-hydration input continuity.
explicitGaps.requiredDisposition: Keep the SSG contract and record any remaining browser-only hydration check before claiming equivalent protection.

explicitGaps.reason: The low-quality canonical route proves mesh consumption, but does not recreate the high-quality lantern shadow-caster removal scene.
explicitGaps.requiredDisposition: Retain the deterministic invalidation contract and require a separate human or approved canonical observation before claiming pixel/shadow parity.

explicitGaps.reason: Macro map and F3 diagnostics are outside C0-C5 and hidden telemetry is not equivalent to their visible UI at narrow viewports.
explicitGaps.requiredDisposition: Lower their data rules to owned contracts; keep visible map/diagnostics behavior as an explicit acceptance gap unless scope is amended.

explicitGaps.reason: The game route consumes production assets but does not open the asset workbench, exercise IndexedDB editing, or inspect every animation/appearance.
explicitGaps.requiredDisposition: Keep manifest/codec/storage contracts and record the workbench and visual matrix as product-specific gaps.

explicitGaps.reason: The canonical browser route is deliberately model-free and does not use provider credentials, PG, WebSocket, or three resident roles.
explicitGaps.requiredDisposition: Keep protocol/host integration tests; run opt-in external evidence separately and never count a skipped run as PASS.
